title: An Evaluation of Time-Trial-Based Predictions of VO2max and Recommended Training Paces for Collegiate and Recreational Runners
publisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: The study tested Jack Daniels' VDOT Running Calculator in NCAA Division 1 track athletes (n = 11) and recreational runners (n = 9) using indoor 5 km time trials.
VDOT underestimated VO2max in athletes (t(10) = -6.00, p < 0.001, d = 1.75) and recreational runners (t(8) = -8.96, p < 0.001, d = 3.44).
The VDOT-VO2max difference was significantly greater in recreational runners than in athletes (p = 0.0031, d = 1.59); reported error was about 4.7% in athletes and 9.2% in recreational runners.
Recommended interval pace (pIN) was slower than the pace at VO2max in recreational runners (d = 1.76) but not different in athletes.
Recommended threshold pace (pTH) was faster than measured lactate threshold pace in athletes (d = 1.49) but not different in recreational runners.
The authors concluded that pTH can be confidently used for threshold training regardless of ability, while pIN may not be optimal for improving VO2max in recreational runners.
The authors advised practitioners to interpret VDOT with caution because it may underestimate VO2max.
